text: Store supplies in your bunker before heading into dangerous territory. Gear left in storage stays out of the fight.
Watch food and water as well as health. A long trip needs more than ammunition.
The heal shortcut uses a medkit from your inventory. Check your supplies before you need one.
A bed can become your respawn point. Choose one near the area you plan to explore.
Sleeping advances time. A bed can help you wait for daylight before setting out.
A flashlight makes dark interiors easier to search. Night vision is an alternative if you find the right headgear.
Death can leave your carried equipment behind. Secure valuables before taking a risk.
Backpacks increase carrying space. Equip one before a long scavenging trip.
A chest rig provides an additional primary weapon slot.
Auto Sort combines compatible stacks and rearranges your inventory to free up space.
Quick-transfer moves items between your inventory and an open container. Its shortcut is shown in the controls.
Aim at an unlocked container to use quick loot. Open the full inventory when you need to organize equipment.
Take All collects what fits. Make room in your inventory if a container still has useful supplies.
Drag compatible ammunition onto a magazine in your inventory to fill it. Check the weapon description for the correct type.
Trading cards are found out in the world. Collect them for permanent bonuses and view them in your collection.
Cover breaks line of sight. Change position when enemies start working around your cover.
Lean around a corner to aim while exposing less of yourself.
Crouching and going prone change how you move through a fight. Keep a clear route back to cover.
A gun can also be used for a melee strike. A close-range hit can give you room to retreat.
Magazines keep their remaining rounds. Reloading does not turn every spare magazine into a full one.
Revolvers and break-action shotguns load cartridges directly. They do not use detachable magazines.
Missile launchers load missiles directly. Tasers use batteries. Neither needs a detachable magazine.
An intact gas pump can refill a flamethrower canister. Exploded pumps are no use for refueling.
Legendary enemies are marked with stars. More stars mean a tougher fight and better rewards.
A weapon's rarity affects its performance. Inspect its stats and legendary effect before choosing what to carry.
Use a weapon workbench to change compatible attachments and apply unlocked camos.
Weapon challenges unlock new finishes. Check your progress at the workbench.
Once a mannequin becomes aggressive, watching it will not stop its charge.
A parked car is not always safe cover. Damaged vehicles can catch fire and explode.
The largest enemies can pick up vehicles. Staying in the driver's seat will not make you untouchable.
Locations appear on the map after you discover them. Discovery also awards a little experience.
Set a waypoint on the map to help plan a route through the world.
The map marks your last driven vehicle. Use it to find your way back after exploring on foot.
Check small camps and roadside stops between towns. Useful supplies are not always inside large buildings.
Dungeons can be much larger than they first appear. Bring supplies for the return trip as well as the entrance.
Deep dungeons hold dangerous enemies and valuable rewards. Expect a difficult opponent near the end.
Locks have different difficulty tiers. Better-protected containers can hold more valuable loot.
Some POIs contain friendly travelers, traders or people with work to offer. Look before you shoot.
Check your fuel before a long drive. Carry a gas can when exploring far from a reliable supply.
A car key belongs to a particular vehicle. Search the glove box; the owner may have left it behind.
A locked car may need lockpicking first and hotwiring afterward if you do not have its key.
Rain builds up on the windshield. Use the wipers to keep a clear view of the road.
Adjust your driving seat to get a better view of the road and dashboard. The controls menu lists the shortcuts.
If a parked vehicle gets wedged in the terrain, try its flip interaction to help free it.
Companions try to ride with you. If there is not enough room, nearby vehicles can let the rest follow.
With a waypoint and a companion, taking a passenger seat can let your companion handle the driving.
An RV offers more than transport. Its beds, seating and separate storage can support life on the road.
Retract an RV's slide-outs before driving. The extra living space is intended for stops.
Parking lots offer a paid service to bring one of your owned vehicles to the lot.
Vehicles stored in your bunker garage become owned vehicles. Large vehicles occupy more than one bay.
Trading and completing contracts improve settlement reputation. Attacking or stealing can turn a welcome into a warning.
High reputation can earn settlement membership. At the highest reputation, leadership opens up more opportunities.
Companion perks increase the number of people you can take along. Send others somewhere safe when your party is full.
Assigned RV bunks give companions a home on the road. Check your sleeping arrangements before leaving town.
Use the entrance terminal to enter build mode, move furniture and purchase expansions.
Bunker furniture costs scrap to build. Keep some material in reserve for your next improvement.
Canadian merchants use Canadian dollars. The currency exchange in Toronto lets you exchange money at a changing rate.
It is autumn 2030. Two years have passed since the nuclear attacks of September 2028.
America collapsed. The rest of the world did not. Beyond the border, ordinary life continues.
Bellwether was a highway service plaza. Now its rooms, counters and parking spaces shelter a community.
Mara Finch keeps people alive with limited supplies. Even a good medic cannot be everywhere at once.
For Ivo Bell, a repair is a promise kept: one more heater, one more light, one more day.
Syracuse still has the shape of a city. Familiar streets lead past buildings whose uses have changed completely.
Shopping centers once gathered crowds to spend money. Some now gather survivors looking for medicine, shelter and news.
The old canal corridor still connects communities. Keeping a route open takes tools, labor and people willing to return tomorrow.
The Lockkeepers grew out of canal workers, mechanics and freight crews. Their workshops keep more than engines running.
Della Voss counts work in obligations as much as hours. Every working machine has somebody behind it.
The Civic Guard draws from surviving military and emergency personnel. Security and organized manpower are its strongest resources.
Captain Elias Rook knows how to hold a line. Deciding which line deserves to be held is harder.
The Freeholds are independent farming and woodland communities. Food, guides and safehouses give them strength beyond their size.
Hannah Pike was a ranger before the collapse. She trusts what people do more than what they promise.
Boat crews, couriers and document brokers form the Night Ferry. The routes they know can be more valuable than the cargo.
Some people on the water rescue strangers. Others see desperation as a market. A crossing and a guarantee are different things.
The Northbank Mission is a Canadian civilian relief organization. Its work includes treatment, evacuation and tracing separated families.
Relief workers face limits of beds, transport and access. A place can be safe and still struggle to welcome everyone at once.
Toronto is a living city. Its lights are maintained by people who expect tomorrow to arrive.
Lake Ontario separates more than shorelines now. Across the water lies a country whose institutions still function.
Survivors remember jobs, neighbors, errands and ordinary plans. The world before the attacks is still within living memory.
A working heater matters more as autumn deepens. Winter has no interest in who owns the road.
News travels through survivors, radio traffic and fragments of records. A confident report is not always a complete one.
Communities survive through small repeated acts: repairing a pump, sharing a meal, keeping watch so someone else can sleep.
